runtime_version: MonkeyOCRv2 parsing pipeline @ d46699fb on vllm==0.11.2
notes: RUNTIME REPOSITORY CORRECTION: benchmark/v6/candidate-registry.yaml records runtime_source_repository Yuliang-Liu/MonkeyOCR. That is the v1 repository; its README now points at Yuliang-Liu/MonkeyOCRv2 for this checkpoint, and only the v2 repository ships the vLLM registration module (parsing/modeling/modeling_monkeyocrv2_vllm_011.py) that MonkeyOCRv2ForCausalLM needs. This runtime uses the v2 repository at d46699fb6a4c71d61588e4a71fce03bff4f1ba33 (head, 2026-09-03). Lane A3 should carry the correction into model_registry.json.

REVISION: pinned to de7a993bd0f39a97b122dac767e82ae04935bce4, the revision in candidate-registry.yaml. The HF main branch has since moved to 2419139b7bcd3fda2689b2a83167172afba91c8b (2026-08-12), but model.safetensors is byte-identical at both revisions (sha256 0267fdc9...), so the newer commit is documentation only. Verified against the HF API at both revisions on 2026-09-03, and RE-VERIFIED on 2026-09-03 under ARENA_CONTRACT D16 (read-only GET https://huggingface.co/api/models/zenosai/MonkeyOCRv2-B-Parsing/revision/<rev>?blobs=true): de7a993b resolves and carries model.safetensors at 1,755,925,032 bytes with LFS sha256 0267fdc991c9be02cf1b60405f77fe0629d084970ad9d6d08163feda3d470284; 2419139b (now the head of main, lastModified 2026-08-12) carries the byte-identical file. runtime.json's de7a993b is therefore right and stands; model_registry.json's 2419139b is the derived copy that is wrong, and lane R copies this value. Pinning the registry revision keeps the two documents consistent at no cost in weights.

DFLASH IS DELIBERATELY OFF. The card and the v2 README advertise MonkeyOCRv2-B-Parsing-DFlash for up to ~2x faster inference through speculative decoding, and serve.py can enable it with --draft-model. It is NOT used here: DFlash needs vLLM >= 0.25.1 and CUDA >= 12.9, it is a different checkpoint plus a different serving stack, and speculative decoding is a different condition from the baseline the vendor's own MDPBench number was measured on. It stays a documented follow-up, not a substitution.

OFFICIAL PIPELINE, NOT A HAND-ROLLED PROMPT: the parsing path is two stages - a LAYOUT pass over the whole page, then per-block recognition with the block's own prompt (Text/Title/Formula/Table/...). Those prompts are data inside parsing/core_runner.py::ALL_PROMPT, and this runtime drives core_runner rather than reimplementing them. prompt_id monkeyocrv2_b_official_pipeline_prompts_v1 therefore registers the pipeline identity (repo + revision), not one prompt string; lane A4 should record it that way. Sampling in the official path is temperature 0 with no top_p unless a repeat retry fires, and retry_repeat is off here because retries belong to the controller (masterplan 15.9).
max_pixels 1003520 is parse.py's default; larger pages are resized proportionally by the official preprocessor, so the arena does no resizing of its own for this model.
http_max_retries is 0, against parse.py's default of 5: the adapter contract forbids retries inside the adapter.

DEPENDENCY OMISSION, stated rather than silent: parsing/requirements.txt pins gradio==5.30.0 and pypdfium2==5.10.1. Only pypdfium2 is installed. gradio is imported by demo/gradio_demo.py alone; core_runner.py does not import it (its imports are torch, requests, PIL, tqdm and modeling.modeling_preprocessor). Pulling the gradio dependency tree into a headless worker would add unpinned transitive packages to a pinned image for no inference benefit.

VRAM BASIS: 1,755,925,032 B of safetensors plus 293 MB of preprocessor .pth files = 2.05 GB of weights, on top of serve.py's own defaults (--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5, --max-model-len 16384, --max-num-seqs 128). 24 GB is a comfortable floor that matches the 4090 pool masterplan 13.3 assigns; the canary measures peak VRAM and decides whether a smaller device or a higher concurrency is right.

Masterplan 47 H5 is the hypothesis this runtime tests: whether MonkeyOCRv2 is strong on photographed and multilingual-like difficulty. The card's 17-language and MDPBench 83.3 claims are quoted, not reproduced.

PROMPT KIND toolkit (ARENA_CONTRACT D34). There is no single prompt string: the vendor pipeline picks a prompt per detected block from core_runner.ALL_PROMPT. The registry file for prompt_id holds a canonical rendering of that mapping - the ARENA_CONTRACT section 2 canonical JSON of the mapping - sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True, no trailing newline - produced by adapter.render_prompt_mapping and already written by lane R. At runtime_revision d46699fb6a4c71d61588e4a71fce03bff4f1ba33 the mapping has 11 keys (Caption, END2END, Formula, LAYOUT, List-item, Page-footer, Page-header, Section-header, Table, Text, Title) and renders to 831 bytes hashing to sha256:3384d4732fd91113b9f7989e488dba575f65225d745a30b797364e12df47dca4, which is what prompt_registry/sha256.json records. adapter.load reads ALL_PROMPT out of the installed toolkit, hashes the rendering and fails closed on any mismatch with the registry.

Framework-floor audit (2026-09-03, after the GLM-OCR canary died on an unrecognised model_type): the required framework floor, what the pinned base image actually ships, the action taken and the evidence URLs are recorded in provenance.json under framework_floor_audit. bootstrap.sh asserts the pinned framework versions and that the framework recognises this checkpoint's architecture before anything starts.
